- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for downward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; apply a 2–5 day lag correction, reducing forecast by 2–5% per day.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; check for mean reversion in 7–14 day window and adjust forecast downward if sentiment reversal is confirmed.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings; apply a 10–15 day smoothing filter to reduce volatility amplification.
- If sentiment is high but price history shows no recent trend, model may overfit; use 18-day moving average as baseline for correction.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is flat, model often predicts minor drift; assume 0.5–1% mean reversion per week unless sentiment shifts.
